land.text: Laconia, the Eurotas valley: Sparta's own land at the end of the Dark Age

predecessors.note: The Sparta infobox dates the foundation to 'Greek Dark Ages c.900 BC'; the project draws the Dark Age as a culture and starts the Greek states in -800, so Sparta is drawn from -800.

land.text: Laconia without the coastal cities: Sparta 'forced into' the Achaean League by Philopoemen in 192 BC after Nabis was overthrown

successors.note: The Sparta infobox says 'Annexed by Achaean League: 188 BC' while the body gives 192 BC; the League of Free Laconians (the coastal cities, independent under Achaean protection from 195) has no dossier and is drawn as Achaean tint at most.

capitals.name: Sparta (Sparti)
capitals.note: Infobox coordinates 37°04′55″N 22°25′25″E; unwalled until Nabis' wall, demolished by Philopoemen in 188.

correction.text: Laconia, the Eurotas valley around Sparta, before the First Messenian War (743–724 BC)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins only in -550, but Sparta is a state of its own from the Dark Age ('Foundation: Greek Dark Ages c.900 BC'). Drawn from -800, the project's Dark Age boundary; before -800 Laconia is Dark Age culture. The Greek City-States shapes -800 and -750 must lose Laconia (their dossier does so).

correction.text: Lacedaemon: Laconia and Messenia, whose people 'were enslaved after defeat' as helots, after the First Messenian War (743–724 BC)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Polis page gives Lacedaemon about 8,400 km2. The Second Messenian War (c. 660–650) is a revolt inside this shape (contest events). The Greek City-States shapes -700..-551 must lose Laconia and Messenia.

correction.text: the shape as drawn: Laconia and Messenia (Lacedaemon) are Sparta's own land; the Tegean (Arcadian) and Corinthian cells inside the shape are allies of the league that 'evolved into the Peloponnesian League' and are drawn as Sparta's tint, not its colour

keyframe_review.note: 15,334 km2 against Lacedaemon's 8,400 km2 on the Polis page (ratio 1.8, within the factor-of-two check): the surplus is allied Arcadia and Corinth. Shape unchanged, status noted.

correction.text: the -550 shape unchanged: Cliopatria has no Peloponnesian League shape for -480..-451, yet nothing on the pages moves Sparta's border between Thermopylae (480) and the First Peloponnesian War

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe filling Cliopatria's gap; the Greek City-States -480 shape already excludes Lacedaemon, so without this keyframe Sparta would vanish for thirty years.

correction.text: the shape as drawn; Boeotia (inside the shape) 'joined as a single unit between 446 and 431 BCE' and Corinth, Megara (rejoined 448), Sicyon, Phlius, Epidaurus and Tegea are league allies drawn as tint; Lacedaemon itself is the colour
the shape as drawn, which includes Attica: 'Athens was forced to join the League in 404' and left in 395; Boeotia (to 395, and again 387–378) and the Isthmus cities are allies drawn as tint

keyframe_review.note: 22,523 km2, the league at its widest after Aegospotami; the ledger ends the Athenian and Boeotian memberships in 395.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, but only for -383..-370: Lacedaemon with Tegea; from -369 Messenia is free (Epaminondas 'freed the helots of Messenia, and rebuilt the ancient city of Messene' in the 370/369 campaign) and the Arcadians have left the league

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria holds this 15,334 km2 shape to -367, two years after the liberation of Messenia; the new keyframe -369 replaces it.

correction.text: Laconia alone, the -366 shape: Messenia gone with the founding of Messene (369), the Arcadians in their own league around Megalopolis (founded 371–368), Sicyon left in 369

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe so that the loss of Messenia is drawn in 369, not 366.

8,991 km2: Laconia alone, close to Lacedaemon-without-Messenia. 'Corinth's departure in 366 BCE effectively ended the League'; Epidaurus and Phlius stayed to 366. From here the dossier is Sparta alone.
10,246 km2 for -350..-338. Cliopatria ends the row in -338 although Sparta 'chose not to join' the League of Corinth and stayed independent; the new keyframes continue it to -192.

correction.text: Laconia as in the -350 shape: Sparta outside the League of Corinth ('except Sparta'); Philip 'proceeded to invade Laconia, devastate much of it and eject the Spartans from various parts' (338), but no page opened names the districts lost

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria puts Laconia into the Greek City-States aggregate from -337; that dossier removes it. The border districts Philip gave to Sparta's neighbours are a confidence-1 ledger event (border band).

correction.text: Laconia with 'Tegea, Mantineia, Caphyae, and Orchomenus in Arcadia', taken by Cleomenes III in 229; Argos and Corinth, held briefly before Sellasia, are undated on the page and left to the ledger

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for Cleomenes III's war (229/228–222). Tripoli stands for the Tegea–Mantineia plain (both within 15 km of it); 'Tegea' and 'Mantineia' are reported to the gazetteer.

correction.text: Laconia alone: after Sellasia (summer 222) Sparta was 'confined' to Laconia; 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus to Macedon', Mantinea and Telphusa taken by Antigonus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Argos, given to Nabis by Macedon during the Second Macedonian War (200–196), is a ledger event.

correction.text: Laconia without the coast: Flamininus made Nabis 'give the coastal Laconian cities autonomy and give them his fleet'; 'Laconian coastal cities become independent under Achean protection as League of Free Laconians'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Gytheio and Monemvasia (reported to the gazetteer) stand for the Free Laconian coast; the war's year is 195 BC (infobox).

region.text: Laconia, the Eurotas valley around Sparta

ledger.note: -800: Sparta, a Dorian state in the Eurotas valley. The infobox dates the foundation to 'Greek Dark Ages c.900 BC'; Herodotus' Dorians 'marched into the Peloponnese' and 'subjugated the local tribes'. The year is the project's Dark Age boundary, not the page's.

724: Messenia conquered; its people become helots. 'First Messenian War: 743–724 BC'; the helots 'came from Messenia and Lakonia and were enslaved after defeat'. Messenia is taken from the Messenian polity, part of the Greek City-States aggregate before 724.

660: the Messenians rise; the Second Messenian War. The page dates it 'c. 660–650 BC' (not the 685–668 of older handbooks). Rule 5 would give the rebels their own hatched colour; no rebel dossier is written (see notes).
650: the Messenian revolt crushed; Messenia remains helot land until 369.

556: Tegea, Sparta's first ally. 'Tegea was the first ally of Sparta in the alliance that evolved into the Peloponnesian League', after the 'bones policy' sponsored by the ephor Chilon c. 556 BCE. League members are drawn as Sparta's tint (rule 4).
550: Corinth joins the league ('Corinth joined c. 550'); 'By the 540s, Sparta had alliances with the Peloponnesian cities except Argos and the Achaean cities'.
550: Elis, 'one of the earliest members'. The page gives no year for Elis; the league's c. 550 is used.

550: Mantinea in the league. 'Mantinea, Phlius, Corinth, Epidaurus, and the Argolid cities followed Tegea's model, largely out of fear of Argos'; the page gives no year for Mantinea, so the league's c. 550 is used.

550: Sicyon in the league. 'Mantinea, Phlius, Corinth, Epidaurus, and the Argolid cities followed Tegea's model, largely out of fear of Argos'; the page gives no year for Sicyon, so the league's c. 550 is used.

550: Epidaurus in the league. 'Mantinea, Phlius, Corinth, Epidaurus, and the Argolid cities followed Tegea's model, largely out of fear of Argos'; the page gives no year for Epidaurus, so the league's c. 550 is used.

550: Phlius in the league. 'Mantinea, Phlius, Corinth, Epidaurus, and the Argolid cities followed Tegea's model, largely out of fear of Argos'; the page gives no year for Phlius, so the league's c. 550 is used.

550: Troezen in the league. 'Mantinea, Phlius, Corinth, Epidaurus, and the Argolid cities followed Tegea's model, largely out of fear of Argos'; the page gives no year for Troezen, so the league's c. 550 is used.

region.text: the plain of Thyrea (Thyreatis) on the Argive border

ledger.note: 546: Thyrea won from Argos. After the duel of the 300 champions ('roughly 546 BC') Argos sent its full army and 'The Spartans won a decisive victory and as a result gained control of Thyreatis'. Argos is a polis of the Greek City-States aggregate; 'Thyreatis' is reported to the gazetteer.
519: Megara 'possibly joined c. 519 BCE'.
461: 'Megara left the League again in 461' and allied with Athens (First Peloponnesian War).
457: Troezen 'left for Athens in 457'.
448: Megara back in the league ('It rejoined in 448'); the Thirty Years' Peace returned 'Megara... to the Peloponnesian League'.
446: Boeotia joins. 'Boeotia/Thebes joined as a single unit between 446 and 431 BCE'; the earliest year of the page's span is used.
446: Troezen 'rejoined following the Thirty Years' Peace' (winter 446–445).
421: 'Mantinea defected in 421 BCE' after the Peace of Nicias.
420: Elis 'left in 420 BCE'.
418: Mantineia 'rejoined after its 418 defeat' at the first battle of Mantinea.

region.text: Decelea, the fort in northern Attica

ledger.note: 413: Decelea fortified. Sparta 'broke the peace in 413 BC' and 'fortified Decelea, near Athens, on Alcibiades' advice'; the Decelean War. Hatched (rule 4); the Athenian dossier records the same event with the roles reversed. 'Decelea' is reported to the gazetteer.

region.text: the island cities of the former Athenian empire under Spartan harmosts

ledger.counterpart: Aegean cities of the former Delian League
ledger.note: 404: the Spartan hegemony over the Aegean. 'Spartan hegemony over Athens and its allies' (infobox); the islands are drawn as Sparta's tint until Cnidus. Ionia is not included: 'In 412 BC... the Persian reconquest of most of Ionia'.
404: the occupation of Decelea ends with Athens' surrender on 25 April 404 BC.

404: Athens, defeated, is 'forced to join the League in 404'; the Thirty Tyrants, 'a reactionary regime set up by Sparta'. The Peloponnesian War page: 'Sparta took over the Athenian empire and kept all its tribute revenues for itself'.
400: Elis 'was forced back c. 400 BCE' after the Spartan–Elean war.
395: Athens leaves the league with the Corinthian War ('Athens left in 395 BCE').
395: 'Corinth also left in 395 BCE because of the Corinthian War'; Corinth and Argos later merged their citizen bodies.
395: 'Thebes left in 395 BCE' and fought Sparta at Haliartus.

ledger.counterpart: Aegean cities of the former Delian League
ledger.note: 394: Cnidus ends Spartan sea power: 'the Spartan fleet was essentially wiped from the sea' and Spartan garrisons were expelled 'from several Ionian and Aegean cities'.
387: Corinth 'returned to Sparta under the King's Peace of 387 BCE'; 'Argos and Corinth ended their experiment in shared government'.
387: the King's Peace. 'Thebes was required to disband the Boeotian League'; 'Sparta's own Peloponnesian League was exempt'. Thebes 'likely returned after 387 BCE' (Peloponnesian League page).

region.text: the Cadmea, the citadel of Thebes

ledger.note: 383: Phoebidas seizes the Cadmea. 'The Cadmea (Theban acropolis) was seized by the Spartan commander Phoebidas', dated 383 by the page (382 in the Thebes page), 'on the way to the 382 campaign' against Olynthus. Hatched; Thebes is then a polis of the aggregate.

379: Olynthus brought into the league: members included 'Olynthos and Thrace, which had recently been conquered' (the Spartan campaign 'against it ran 382–379 BC'). 'Chalcidice' is reported to the gazetteer.

379: Thebes freed. 'Pelopidas and companions liberated Thebes in 379 BC by assassinating the pro-Spartan tyrants'; the garrison surrendered. From this year Thebes has its own dossier (sacred-band-of-thebes).
378: 'Thebes left the Peloponnesian League for good in 378'; the Boeotian War (378–371) begins.
371: after Leuctra 'decisively shook its control of the League members' the Chalcidian cities are no longer Spartan allies; the page gives no year for their departure.
370: the Arcadians leave: 'The Arcadians left the League around 370 BCE to form the Arcadian League', founded around Megalopolis.
370: Mantineia, 'reconstituted after Leuctra', leaves with the other Arcadians for the Arcadian League.

region.text: Laconia 'down to the port of Gythium'

ledger.note: 370: Epaminondas invades Laconia. 'The Thebans and their allies ravaged Laconia, down to the port of Gythium'; 'The Spartans, unwilling to engage the massive army in battle, simply defended their city'. Winter 370/369.
369: the Thebans leave Laconia for Messenia and Arcadia; Sparta keeps Laconia.

region.text: Messenia, the helots freed; Messene founded on Mount Ithome

ledger.note: 369: Messenia free. Epaminondas 'built the new city of Messene on the site in 369 BC over the ruins of Ithome' and 'invited the return of the previous inhabitants'. The new Messenian state has no Cliopatria row: it is drawn in the Greek City-States aggregate, in Theban tint while Thebes' ally (369–362).
369: 'Sicyon remained a member without interruption until 369'; Sicyon 'became allied to Thebes' in Epaminondas' second invasion.

366: the Peloponnesian League ends. 'Corinth's departure in 366 BCE effectively ended the League'; Epidaurus 'remained a member without interruption until 366' and Phlius' oligarchs 'remained loyal to Sparta until 366'. Corinth's own exit year is the page's.

366: the Peloponnesian League ends. 'Corinth's departure in 366 BCE effectively ended the League'; Epidaurus 'remained a member without interruption until 366' and Phlius' oligarchs 'remained loyal to Sparta until 366'. Epidaurus's own exit year is the page's.

366: the Peloponnesian League ends. 'Corinth's departure in 366 BCE effectively ended the League'; Epidaurus 'remained a member without interruption until 366' and Phlius' oligarchs 'remained loyal to Sparta until 366'. Phlius's own exit year is the page's.

366: the Peloponnesian League ends. 'Corinth's departure in 366 BCE effectively ended the League'; Epidaurus 'remained a member without interruption until 366' and Phlius' oligarchs 'remained loyal to Sparta until 366'. Elis's own exit year is not given by the page; the league's end is used.

366: the Peloponnesian League ends. 'Corinth's departure in 366 BCE effectively ended the League'; Epidaurus 'remained a member without interruption until 366' and Phlius' oligarchs 'remained loyal to Sparta until 366'. Megara's own exit year is not given by the page; the league's end is used.

366: the Peloponnesian League ends. 'Corinth's departure in 366 BCE effectively ended the League'; Epidaurus 'remained a member without interruption until 366' and Phlius' oligarchs 'remained loyal to Sparta until 366'. Troezen's own exit year is not given by the page; the league's end is used.

region.text: the frontier districts of Laconia given to Sparta's neighbours

ledger.note: 338: Philip II in Laconia. 'In 338 BC, Philip II invaded and devastated much of Laconia' and (Philip II page) 'eject[ed] the Spartans from various parts'; no page opened names the districts (Dentheliatis, Belminatis, Sciritis and Thyreatis in the handbooks), so a one-cell border band stands for them. [Reviewer eu-01-c, 2026-10-18: border_band year -337 changed to -338: the Cliopatria peloponnesian-league row has no shape in -337]

region.text: Megalopolis in Arcadia, besieged by Agis III

ledger.note: 331: Agis III's war. 'Agis laid siege to Megalopolis in 331 BC. A Macedonian army under Antipater defeated the Spartan-led force, and Agis was killed.' 'Megalopolis' is reported to the gazetteer.
331: Antipater's victory ends the war in the same year; no land changes hands.

region.text: Tegea, Mantineia, Caphyae and Orchomenus in Arcadia

ledger.note: 229: Cleomenes III takes eastern Arcadia. 'In 229 BC, Cleomenes took the important cities Tegea, Mantineia, Caphyae, and Orchomenus in Arcadia' (by treachery or invitation, the page says the sources disagree). The cities are poleis of the aggregate; their league allegiance in 229 is not on the page.

225: Argos and Corinth go over to Cleomenes. 'The Corinthians did surrender the city to Cleomenes' after he 'seized the rugged area above the city's theatre' at Argos; the page gives no years, so the conventional 225 is a bridging date (confidence 1).

region.text: 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus to Macedon'; Mantinea and Telphusa taken by Antigonus

ledger.note: 222: Sellasia. 'In the summer of 222 BC... Cleomenes fought the Achaeans and the Macedonians at Sellasia, where the Spartans were routed'; 'Antigonus entered Sparta triumphantly, its first foreign conqueror', revoked the reforms and 'restored the ephors'. Sparta 'confined' to Laconia. [Reviewer eu-01-c, 2026-10-18: counterpart slug antigonid-macedonia corrected to antigonid-dynasty, the dossier that carries the Antigonid Macedonia row]

region.text: Argos, back to the Achaean League

ledger.note: 222: Argos returns to the Achaean League after Sellasia. [Reviewer eu-01-c, 2026-10-18: confidence 2 lowered to 1: the Cleomenean War page gives no year for Argos returning to the Achaeans]

region.text: Argos, handed to Nabis by Philip V

ledger.note: 197: Argos given to Nabis. 'Macedon gave Argos to Sparta during the Second Macedonian War (200–196 BC)'; 'Nabis accepted and received control over Argos'. The page gives no year inside 200–196 (confidence 1). [Reviewer eu-01-c, 2026-10-18: counterpart slug antigonid-macedonia corrected to antigonid-dynasty]
195: the war against Nabis. Flamininus 'led his force of 50,000 men to Sparta'; Nabis had to surrender Argos: 'Argos to the Achaean League' (infobox).

region.text: the coastal Laconian cities, Gythium first

ledger.note: 195: the Laconian coast freed. Nabis must 'give the coastal Laconian cities autonomy and give them his fleet'; 'Laconian coastal cities become independent under Achean protection as League of Free Laconians'. No dossier exists for the Free Laconians (see notes).

region.text: Laconia without the coast: Sparta made 'a member state of the League'

ledger.note: 192: Sparta forced into the Achaean League. 'Sparta was forced into it by Philopoemen in 192 BC after Nabis was overthrown' (the infobox says 188; the Nabis page gives no year). After 146 Sparta became 'a free city under Roman rule' (Achaean War page: 'autonomy was granted to some cities, including Athens and Sparta').

wars.name: First Messenian War
wars.outcome: Spartan victory: Messenia conquered and its people reduced to helots.
wars.note: 'First Messenian War: 743–724 BC' (Sparta page); the Messenians are a polity of the Greek City-States aggregate.

wars.name: Second Messenian War
wars.outcome: The helot revolt crushed; Messenia stays Spartan.
wars.note: 'c. 660–650 BC' on the Sparta page; older dates (685–668) are not the page's.

wars.name: Battle of the 300 Champions
wars.outcome: Indecisive duel, then a decisive Spartan victory over the full Argive army; Sparta 'gained control of Thyreatis'.
wars.note: Argos challenged Sparta to a rematch in 420 BC; 'Sparta declined'.

wars.name: First Peloponnesian War
wars.outcome: Thirty Years' Peace (winter 446–445): 'Megara was returned to the Peloponnesian League', 'Troezen and Achaea became independent', Athens gave up 'all possessions in the Peloponnese'.

wars.name: Peloponnesian War

zones.text: the Aegean and Ionian cities of the Athenian empire

wars.outcome: 'Spartan victory'; 'Dissolution of the Delian League; Spartan hegemony over Athens and its allies'. Athens surrendered on 25 April 404 BC.
wars.note: Dates '4 April 431 – 25 April 404 BC'. Thebes is a polis of the aggregate until 379; its slug is given for the renderer's convenience.

wars.name: Corinthian War

zones.text: the Aegean cities freed from Spartan garrisons after Cnidus (394)

wars.outcome: The King's Peace 'dictated by the Achaemenid King Artaxerxes II in 387 BC': Asia Minor, Clazomenae and Cyprus to Persia; Lemnos, Imbros and Scyros to Athens; 'All other Greek cities were to be autonomous'; 'Thebes disbanded its league'.

wars.name: Boeotian War
wars.outcome: Theban victory at Leuctra (371), which 'decisively shook its control of the League members'.
wars.note: 'General fighting resumed in 378 BC, starting the Boeotian War (378–371 BC)'.

wars.name: Theban invasions of the Peloponnese
wars.outcome: Messenia lost for good; the Arcadian League founded; the Battle of Mantinea (4 July 362) a 'Theban tactical victory' and 'Strategic draw' in which Epaminondas died.

wars.name: Philip II's invasion of Laconia
wars.outcome: Laconia devastated, border districts given to Sparta's neighbours, Sparta itself not taken; Sparta stayed outside the League of Corinth.

wars.name: War of Agis III
wars.outcome: Antipater's victory; Agis killed; no change of borders.

wars.name: Cleomenean War
wars.outcome: 'Achaean and Macedonian victory' at Sellasia (summer 222); 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus to Macedon'; Sparta confined to Laconia and occupied by Antigonus.

wars.name: War against Nabis
wars.outcome: 'Argos to the Achaean League, Laconian coastal cities become independent under Achean protection as League of Free Laconians'; an indemnity over eight years.
wars.note: The infobox also lists Doric Cretans and Argos on Nabis' side.

certainty.note: Ancient frontiers throughout; the Messenian border along Taygetus and the Thyreatis are the only named lines, and the pages give no survey.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Peloponnesian League' row (-550..-338) is in substance Sparta's state (Lacedaemon, about 8,400 km2) plus the allied Arcadian and Isthmus cells; the league itself is an alliance, which rule 4 draws as tint, so this dossier is written as the Spartan state with the league members as vassal_start/vassal_end events (counterpart = the member's name) and the row extended to -800..-192 as the group's scope asks ('Sparta... as states in their own right'). Cliopatria rows to correct: the Peloponnesian League row has a gap -480..-451 (filled by a new keyframe), holds Messenia to -367 (freed 369), and ends in -338 although Sparta stayed outside the League of Corinth; Greek City-States must lose Laconia (-800..-751), Laconia and Messenia (-700..-551) and Laconia again (-337..-193), which that dossier does. Pages that would not settle: the Sparta page dates the Second Messenian War c. 660–650 (not 685–668); Argos and Corinth under Cleomenes are undated on the Cleomenean War page (225 is a bridging date); Argos to Nabis is dated only '200–196'; the Sparta infobox gives 188 for the Achaean annexation against 192 in the text; the Philip II page does not date the Laconian invasion or name the districts lost (handbooks: Dentheliatis, Belminatis, Sciritis, Thyreatis). States needing a dossier from another group or a gap-filler: Messene (369–146, a Messenian state; here it goes to the Greek City-States aggregate), the Arcadian League (370–362), the League of Free Laconians (195 onward, Achaean protection), the Messenian rebels of 660–650 (a rebel state under rule 5 if the reviewer wants it hatched). Gazetteer names used but absent: regions Laconia, Messenia, Elis, Argolid, Thyreatis, Chalcidice; places Tegea, Mantineia, Sikyon, Epidaurus, Phlius, Troezen, Megara, Decelea, Megalopolis, Gytheio, Monemvasia.
